plan.objective: Decide whether to proceed with the new plant investment.

rubric.text: Evaluate the proposed new plant investment.
Compute the NPV and IRR of the cash flows.
Recommend whether to proceed and explain the risks.

analyses.rubric_text: Compute the NPV and IRR of the cash flows.
analyses.why: the wording of this item matches what this analysis is for
analyses.will_produce: the computed result with its derivation and the checks that ran

inputs.name: cashflows
inputs.desc: cash flows, first at t=0 (normally the negative outlay)

analyses.intended_use: The discount rate at which a declared stream of cash flows has a net present value of zero (the IRR, for conventional cash flows).
analyses.unsupported_use: Ranking or choosing between projects; non-conventional cash flows (more than one sign change) where several IRRs can exist; comparing IRRs of projects of unequal scale or life; choosing or assuming a reinvestment rate.
limitations: Single constant rate; IRR ignores project scale and can mislead when comparing projects.
The root is found numerically in the range -99.99% to 1000%; a root outside that range is treated as absent.
Several sign changes block instead of choosing a root.

declared_defaults.question: Root and timing convention
declared_defaults.default_chosen: End-of-period cash flows with the first at t=0, exactly as in npv. The cash flows must change sign once, giving one IRR; several sign changes are refused rather than resolved.
declared_defaults.impact: Non-conventional cash flows have multiple IRRs, so any single answer would be a choice.
